correctness.rationale: Substitution implies p_(2j)=0, p_(2j+1)=1-p_j; no 11 and hence no 0000. Equal length≥4 factors of opposite parity would be all-zero over four letters and are impossible. Same-parity equalities decimate bijectively to equal factors of lengths floor(n/2) and ceil(n/2), producing first possible repeat positions 2R(floor(n/2)) and 2R(ceil(n/2))+1. R is monotone, giving the recurrence. Base positions 2,3,4 determine the two plateau ranges and liminf/limsup. The package checker directly compares the fixed point and first-repeat windows at n=1..512 using complete byte equality and confirms 320 further arithmetic identities.

originality.rationale: The exact length-doubling recurrence and resulting two-plateau formula for the period-doubling fixed-point initial non-repetitive complexity were not stated or directly implied by the inspected primary literature, general occurrence formulas, or competing maximal-window tables. residual_risks: A global first-collision formula could be derivable with further nontrivial minimization from the all-factor occurrence formulas of Huang–Zhang (2014) or related return-word work.

value.rationale: Initial non-repetitive complexity is an established natural invariant quantifying how long the fixed prefix reveals new factors before its first collision. This gives its first all-length exact classification for a canonical primitive automatic substitution, a renormalization law, and exact extremal normalized ratios; it is not an arbitrary finite slice or merely a restated factor table. Prior studies determine this invariant on other classical substitutions and all-factor occurrence positions for this one, but not the reported global prefix optimum.
